result.title: Analysing the Narrative Paradox through Formal Models and Properties in Interactive Narrative
result.summary: Interactive narratives aim to let players influence the unfolding of a story while preserving a coherent and satisfying narrative progression. This creates a central tension, commonly described as the narrative paradox, between player autonomy and narrative control. Experience Managers (EMs) manage the story by determining how the narrative progresses in response to player behaviour. Although this paradox is widely discussed, it is rarely modelled in a way that supports systematic analysis, simulation, and comparison across management strategies. This paper proposes a formal framework for modelling and analysing the narrative paradox as a trade-off between interdependent properties shaped by EM decisions. We represent interactive narrative behaviour through an extended state-transition system in which world states are connected by player actions and system events. From this model, we formalize key properties involved in the paradox such as the player agency, EM controllability, author intent, and robustness, and define quantitative indicators derived from simulated plans. These indicators make it possible to compare EM strategies according to their ability to balance freedom, control, and narrative satisfaction. A case study compares different EM policies, showing how simulations can reveal correlations and conflicts between properties and identify compromise zones in the design space. This work contributes a reusable modelling and analysis framework for studying the narrative paradox and evaluating heterogeneous interactive narratives on shared formal grounds, with a focus on supporting the comparison and testing of EM strategies.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一个形式化框架，用扩展的状态转移系统刻画交互叙事中玩家动作与系统事件如何连接世界状态，并形式化玩家能动性、管理者可控性、作者意图与鲁棒性等性质，再由模拟计划导出量化指标，用于比较不同叙事管理策略在自由与可控之间的折中。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把“自主性 vs 控制”这类相互依赖性质形式化并以模拟指标刻画折中区间的做法，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的计算投入与答案控制之权衡及策略比较提供评价框架线索，但领域为游戏叙事，需核查可迁移性。
